explanation: Compared against the Wikipedia article 'Butson-type Hadamard matrix', section Existence: 'If p is prime and N > 1, then H(p, N) can exist only for N = mp with integer m' (citing Butson, Proc. AMS 13 (1962)). The Lean statement: for p prime and 2 ≤ n, if there exists M with IsButsonHadamard p n M (entries are p-th roots of unity, M·M* = n·I over ℂ), then p ∣ n. The definition matches the article's (entries satisfying z^q = 1 and mutually orthogonal rows), the hypothesis n ≥ 2 is the article's N > 1 (needed since [1] is an H(p, 1)), and the conclusion p ∣ n is N = mp. For p = 2 this gives the true fact that a real Hadamard matrix of order ≥ 2 has even order. Faithful.
